name: Peruvian Pigeon
rangeDescription: Northern peru (subtropical marañón valley) and adjacent southern ecuador
description: Large, rusty pigeon confined to the Marañon drainage of northwestern Peru. Its range may extend to extreme southern Ecuador, but evidence is lacking.

name: Red-breasted Goose
rangeDescription: Breeds low arctic tundra of yamal, gydan, and taymyr peninsulas (northwestern siberia); winters to western and southern black sea and southern caspian sea; prone to vagrancy elsewhere in eurasia
description: Small and stocky rare goose with a small bill. From a distance, appears dark and dull, and often blends into flocks of other geese.

name: Brazza's Martin
rangeDescription: Locally along rivers of southwestern democratic republic of the congo and northeastern angola (lunda)
description: A typical martin with brown upperparts and pale underparts strongly marked with dark streaks. Juvenile is rustier, with a paler chin and throat, and is less boldly streaked below.

name: Sumatran Frogmouth
rangeDescription: Montane forest of sumatra
description: A Sumatran endemic, this medium-sized nightbird is limited to foothill and montane forests between 1200 and 2000 meters, only rarely straying to lower elevations. Nocturnal and difficult to see by day as it perches quietly in the middle levels of forest.

name: Tacarcuna Chlorospingus
rangeDescription: Montane forest of eastern panama and far northwestern colombia
description: Fairly small tanager-like sparrow with an extremely tiny range in Panama. Occurs in humid forests from around 800–1,500 m.

name: Taiga Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Siberia to kamchatka and northern mongolia; winters to borneo
description: Small brown flycatcher with a sharply contrasting black-and-white tail. Breeding male has an orange throat patch surrounded by a faint gray wash.

name: Western Crowned Warbler
rangeDescription: Mountains of eastern afghanistan and kashmir; winters in india
description: Distinctive leaf warbler with two wingbars, green upperparts often contrasting with the gray head and the striking white underparts, a distinct crown stripe, and a long pale bill. Endemic to the Indian Subcontinent.

name: Jelski's Black-Tyrant
rangeDescription: East slope of andes from southeastern ecuador (zamora-chinchipe) southward to central peru (to junín)
description: Rare flycatcher found in cloud forest along the east slope of the Andes in northern and central Peru, barely reaching over the border into southeastern Ecuador. Male is dark sooty gray; female is grayish-olive with pale wingbars and faint streaking below.

name: Violet-tailed Sunbird
rangeDescription: Cameroon to gabon, northeastern angola, central african republic, and northeastern democratic republic of the congo
description: An iridescent sunbird of forest and forest edge, almost always near water. Males are distinctly bicolored: iridescent purple on their tails and heads and white on their bellies, with iridescent green highlights on the wings and orange underwing tufts.

name: Pale-throated Wren-Babbler
rangeDescription: Northern vietnam (northwestern tonkin)
description: Shy inhabitant of dense undergrowth in midddle- to high-altitude forests. Brown and scaly-looking overall with a gray face and pale throat.

name: Peruvian Recurvebill
rangeDescription: Tropical southeastern peru, far northwestern bolivia, and amazonian brazil
description: Reddish-brown bird with a distinctive upturned bill. Found almost exclusively in bamboo thickets, but occasionally also in dense viny areas.

name: White-fronted Wattle-eye
rangeDescription: Lowlands and escarpment of western angola and adjacent southwestern democratic republic of the congo
description: A cute and dumpy black, gray, and white flycatcher-like bird with striking red eye-wattles and white wing-stripes. The sexes differ: male has a broad black chest band and dark gray upperparts; female has completely white underparts and is duller gray above.

name: Inagua Woodstar
rangeDescription: Scrub, riparian areas, and gardens of great and little inagua islands (southern bahamas)
description: A small, long-tailed hummingbird of wooded and scrubby habitats including gardens; most often found feeding on flowers or at hummingbird feeders. Note the male’s iridescent purple throat and forehead plus its long, forked tail.

name: Swainson's Sparrow
rangeDescription: Far northeastern sudan to ethiopia, northern somalia, and north-central kenya
description: A drab sparrow of northeastern Africa. The head and underparts are gray, the wing and back are brown, and the rump is rufous.

name: Malabar Pied-Hornbill
rangeDescription: Mixed forest of southern india and sri lanka
description: A large black-and-white hornbill with a huge bill and casque. The plumage is almost entirely black, but for the white on the belly and the sides of the throat.

name: Ringed Storm-Petrel
rangeDescription: Ranges coastal ecuador to central chile
description: Handsome small seabird of Humboldt Current; not seen from shore, but breeds inland in Atacama Desert where it visits colonies at night to avoid predators. Plumage unlike all other storm-petrels, with black cap and collar, and white underparts contrasting with dark underwings.

name: Scarlet-rumped Trogon
rangeDescription: Lowland forest of malay peninsula, sumatra, and borneo
description: Striking trogon with an extensive blue gape and a similarly-colored patch above the eye. Male has a brilliantly scarlet rump and underparts.

name: Cambodian Laughingthrush
rangeDescription: Southwestern cambodia
description: A chocolate-colored laughingthrush with a dark hood, found solely in the upper reaches of Cambodia’s Cardamom Mountains. Pale blue facial patch behind the eye and bright white patch on the upper neck are diagnostic.

name: Beautiful Sunbird
rangeDescription: Mauritania, senegal, and guinea-bissau eastward to sudan, eritrea, and ethiopia, southward to sierra leone, central nigeria, northern cameroon, central african republic, south sudan, extreme northeastern democratic republic of the congo, uganda, and northwestern kenya
description: A slim, long-billed sunbird in which breeding males and females are very different. Breeding males are mostly dark green with a red-and-yellow band across the underparts.

name: Bornean Leafbird
rangeDescription: Upland forest of northern borneo
description: Accurately-named leaf-green canopy-dweller of Borneo’s central montane forests. Male has a black throat with a blue center and lemon-yellow outline.
